43:   const termById = new Map<string, GlossaryTerm>();

97:   while (i < text.length) {
98:     const ch = text[i];
99:     if (ch === '\\' && (text[i + 1] === '[' || text[i + 1] === ']')) {
100:       plain += text[i + 1];
101:       hadBrackets = true;
102:       i += 2;
103:       continue;
104:     }
105:     if (ch === '[') {

107:       if (close === -1) {
108:         plain += ch;
109:         i += 1;
110:         continue;
111:       }
112:       const display = text.slice(i + 1, close);
113:       let resolveKey = display;
114:       let end = close + 1;
115:       if (text[end] === '[') {
116:         const close2 = text.indexOf(']', end + 1);
117:         if (close2 !== -1) {
118:           resolveKey = text.slice(end + 1, close2);

126:       continue;

133: }

137:  * `tokenizeTags` for the bracket grammar). Returns `hadExplicit: true` the moment any bracket
138:  * construct is found — see `linkifyText` for why that's the signal that turns off the regex

140:  */

145: ): { segments: GlossarySegment[]; hadExplicit: boolean } {

148:     if (t.kind === 'text') return { text: t.value };
149:     const term = resolveExplicitTag(t.resolveKey, matcher);

156:  *  Admin's Validation panel (`validateLibrary`, `apps/server/src/adminLogic.ts`) to surface a

160:   const { tokens } = tokenizeTags(text);
161:   const unresolved: string[] = [];

172:  * rendering top-level sheet text should leave it at the default 0.
173:  *

175:  * contains a tap-target that reopens itself.

178:  * first. **A field containing at least one explicit tag is treated as fully explicit** — the
179:  * regex auto-linker below is skipped for the rest of that field, not just the tagged occurrence.
180:  * That's what makes migrating a field to explicit tags free: no flag, no backfill, a field with
181:  * no brackets behaves exactly as it always has.
182:  */
183: export function linkifyText(
184:   text: string,
185:   matcher: GlossaryMatcher,
186:   depth = 0,
187:   excludeTermId?: string,
188: ): GlossarySegment[] {
189:   if (!text || depth > MAX_DEPTH) return [{ text }];
190: 
191:   const explicit = scanExplicitTags(text, matcher, excludeTermId);
192:   if (explicit.hadExplicit) return explicit.segments.length ? explicit.segments : [{ text: '' }];
193: 
194:   if (!matcher.regex) return [{ text }];
195: 
196:   const segments: GlossarySegment[] = [];
197:   let lastIndex = 0;
198:   matcher.regex.lastIndex = 0;
199:   let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
200:   while ((match = matcher.regex.exec(text))) {
201:     if (match.index > lastIndex) segments.push({ text: text.slice(lastIndex, match.index) });
202:     const term = matcher.termByKey.get(match[0].toLowerCase());
203:     // Excluded (a term's own name inside its own Definition) still renders as plain text —
204:     // only the tap-link is suppressed, the word itself must not disappear from the sentence.
205:     segments.push(term && term.Id !== excludeTermId ? { text: match[0], term } : { text: match[0] });
206:     lastIndex = match.index + match[0].length;
207:   }
208:   if (lastIndex < text.length) segments.push({ text: text.slice(lastIndex) });
209:   return segments.length ? segments : [{ text }];
210: }

110:         continue;

113:       let resolveKey = display;
114:       let end = close + 1;

120:         }
121:       }

123:       flushPlain();
124:       tokens.push({ kind: 'tag', display, resolveKey });
125:       i = end;
126:       continue;
127:     }
128:     plain += ch;
129:     i += 1;

131:   flushPlain();

135: /**
136:  * Scans `text` for explicit glossary tags and resolves each one against `matcher` (see
137:  * `tokenizeTags` for the bracket grammar). Returns `hadExplicit: true` the moment any bracket
138:  * construct is found — see `linkifyText` for why that's the signal that turns off the regex
139:  * auto-linker for the rest of this field, not just the tagged occurrence.
140:  */
141: function scanExplicitTags(
142:   text: string,
143:   matcher: GlossaryMatcher,
144:   excludeTermId?: string,
145: ): { segments: GlossarySegment[]; hadExplicit: boolean } {
146:   const { tokens, hadBrackets } = tokenizeTags(text);
147:   const segments: GlossarySegment[] = tokens.map((t) => {
148:     if (t.kind === 'text') return { text: t.value };
149:     const term = resolveExplicitTag(t.resolveKey, matcher);
150:     return term && term.Id !== excludeTermId ? { text: t.display, term } : { text: t.display };
151:   });
152:   return { segments, hadExplicit: hadBrackets };
153: }
154: 
155: /** Every explicit tag's resolve-key that failed to resolve against `matcher` — used by Content
156:  *  Admin's Validation panel (`validateLibrary`, `apps/server/src/adminLogic.ts`) to surface a
157:  *  typo'd or dangling `[Tag]` at authoring time, per the plan's "an author finds out at authoring
158:  *  time" requirement, rather than it silently rendering as plain text forever. */
159: export function findUnresolvedGlossaryTags(text: string, matcher: GlossaryMatcher): string[] {
160:   const { tokens } = tokenizeTags(text);
161:   const unresolved: string[] = [];
162:   for (const t of tokens) {
163:     if (t.kind === 'tag' && !resolveExplicitTag(t.resolveKey, matcher)) unresolved.push(t.resolveKey);

165:   return unresolved;

169:  * Splits `text` into plain and glossary-matched segments.
170:  *
171:  * `depth` tracks recursion into a term's own Definition (see MAX_DEPTH above) — callers
172:  * rendering top-level sheet text should leave it at the default 0.
173:  *
174:  * `excludeTermId` skips a term when linkifying its own Definition, so a term's bubble never
175:  * contains a tap-target that reopens itself.
176:  *

178:  * first. **A field containing at least one explicit tag is treated as fully explicit** — the
179:  * regex auto-linker below is skipped for the rest of that field, not just the tagged occurrence.
180:  * That's what makes migrating a field to explicit tags free: no flag, no backfill, a field with
181:  * no brackets behaves exactly as it always has.
182:  */

184:   text: string,
185:   matcher: GlossaryMatcher,
186:   depth = 0,
187:   excludeTermId?: string,
188: ): GlossarySegment[] {
189:   if (!text || depth > MAX_DEPTH) return [{ text }];
190: 
191:   const explicit = scanExplicitTags(text, matcher, excludeTermId);
192:   if (explicit.hadExplicit) return explicit.segments.length ? explicit.segments : [{ text: '' }];
193: 
194:   if (!matcher.regex) return [{ text }];

196:   const segments: GlossarySegment[] = [];
197:   let lastIndex = 0;
198:   matcher.regex.lastIndex = 0;
199:   let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
200:   while ((match = matcher.regex.exec(text))) {
201:     if (match.index > lastIndex) segments.push({ text: text.slice(lastIndex, match.index) });
202:     const term = matcher.termByKey.get(match[0].toLowerCase());
203:     // Excluded (a term's own name inside its own Definition) still renders as plain text —
204:     // only the tap-link is suppressed, the word itself must not disappear from the sentence.
205:     segments.push(term && term.Id !== excludeTermId ? { text: match[0], term } : { text: match[0] });

207:   }
208:   if (lastIndex < text.length) segments.push({ text: text.slice(lastIndex) });
209:   return segments.length ? segments : [{ text }];
210: }
